title: Bounded morphisms of intuitionistic propositional models
summary: Preserve constructive truth along specified world maps, distinguish forward extension from lifting futures, and transfer countermodels and frame validities.
abstract: A model can split one possible future into two copies without changing what is known at the original world. The same formulas can also survive when a model is restricted to all futures of one point. Bounded morphisms explain both phenomena: they keep atom information and match the possible extensions in both directions. We prove that every constructive propositional formula has the same truth value at corresponding worlds, then use this to transport countermodels. Pulling valuations back also transfers validities between frames. Small examples show why monotonicity alone misses future information, and why preserving truth in matching models differs from preserving every possible valuation on a frame.
